title: Junior → AI System Architect
intro: The same shape applies to every path — only the technical depth changes. Each rung is a step up in the size of the ambiguity you are trusted to absorb, not a count of years served.
closing: The last stage of every path points at this same ladder. There are not seven architect tracks: one sits above all of them, because at that level the job becomes system-level judgement rather than language or framework specifics.

levels.title: Junior
levels.guidance: Follow the roadmap exactly, complete every project listed, and focus on correctness over cleverness.
responsibilities: Work inside patterns the codebase already establishes
Complete every project on the path rather than sampling them
Optimise for correctness over cleverness
Put work up for review early, while it is still cheap to change
levels.entryNote: The entry rung. The bar here is finishing things, not designing them.
separators: Can read an existing codebase and add to it without breaking its conventions
Finishes what gets started, including the unglamorous last ten percent
Knows when to ask rather than guessing for another two hours

levels.title: Mid-level
levels.guidance: Start making architecture choices on your own projects — why RAG vs fine-tuning, why this vector DB, why this framework.
responsibilities: Take a feature from requirement to production without being sequenced through it
Ship one complete project solo, start to finish
Choose between competing approaches and defend the choice
Notice when an established pattern does not fit, and say so
separators: Chooses the approach instead of implementing the one handed over
Can justify RAG versus fine-tuning, this vector database, this framework
Owns a whole feature rather than a well-specified slice of one

levels.title: Senior
levels.guidance: Think in tradeoffs, not tutorials — reliability, cost, latency and security become your job rather than an afterthought. Mentor others.
responsibilities: Design systems rather than features
Carry reliability, cost, latency and security as first-class concerns
Mentor juniors and raise the ceiling of the people nearby
State the tradeoff plainly when there is no clean answer
separators: Reliability, cost, latency and security are the job, not an afterthought
Thinks in tradeoffs rather than tutorials — there is rarely one right answer
Output now includes other people getting better, not only shipped code

levels.title: Lead / Staff
levels.guidance: Own cross-team technical direction, write design docs before code, and evaluate build-vs-buy.
responsibilities: Set technical direction across more than one team
Write the design document before the code exists
Review other people's architecture, not only their diffs
Run build-versus-buy decisions with real numbers attached
separators: Scope crosses team boundaries rather than stopping at one
The design document comes before the implementation, not after it
Evaluates whether to build the thing at all

levels.title: AI System Architect
levels.focus: Own org-wide AI strategy and platform
levels.scope: Diagrams and decision records over code; cost, risk and scale owner
levels.guidance: Own the end-to-end system — model and provider selection, scaling strategy, governance, cost ceilings, and how AI investment ties to business value. Works in diagrams and decision records as much as code.
responsibilities: Own model and provider selection across the whole organisation
Set scaling strategy and the cost ceilings that go with it
Own governance and risk as named outcomes
Tie AI investment to business value in terms the business recognises
Work in diagrams and decision records as much as in code
separators: Scope is the organisation, not a set of teams
Cost, risk and scale are owned outcomes rather than inputs someone hands over
The primary artefact is a decision record; code is no longer the main one
